advances: A necessary condition for an actual local fixed-budget volume maximum with positive polytopal fibers. No bound on the signed Euler offset or global mixed-depth claim follows.

proof:
Inner erosion is obtained by shifting all unit facet offsets by $-t$. For small positive $t$ every original facet persists by shifting a relative interior point inward by $tn_F$, where all other inequalities stay strict. Each candidate vertex comes from an independent set of original normals and is affine in $t$. Finitely many affine feasibility and incidence tests are constant for sufficiently small positive $t$. Thus the resulting normal fan is fixed and uses the original facet normals. It refines the old fan because each new vertex converges to an old vertex, and its active normals are active at the limit. Its supports are affine in $t$ along the common refinement.

On the simplicial refinement the ray supports define linear pieces. The condition that each linear piece lie below the prescribed value at every ray is equivalent to convexity: the resulting function is the maximum of the pieces, hence a support function. Each anchored compatibility inequality is linear on fan cones, so it suffices to check it at the rays and at the finitely many vertices of the polytope of anchored weights. Requiring linearity on a fiber's own fan adds only linear equations. It allows no facet normals outside its rays, since a fan on which a support is linear must refine that body's normal fan. The original positive-area facets persist under small offset changes by the strict relative-interior slack argument. For the resulting finite homogeneous inequalities $Ah\ge0$, the radial cone at $h$ is exactly $\{\delta:A_0\delta\ge0\}$ by strict slack of the inactive rows. Small radial perturbations remain full-dimensional because they preserve positive minimum width.

Common erosion preserves compatibility: if $\sum_w p_w K_w\subset K_z$ and $\sum_w p_w=1$, then $\sum_w p_w(K_w\ominus tB_d)+tB_d\subset\sum_w p_w K_w\subset K_z$. Its radial velocity $e$ has $e_z(n_F)=-1$ at each original facet. Apply the strip argument of 7a5ea4f8a4c5094c to each singleton fiber, with its own one-row-per-facet representation and fixed cap plane. The body speed there is $\delta_z(n_F)$, and the cap threshold speed is zero. This gives all stated derivative terms including the two coincidence signs. In particular every true cap derivative is one of the finite covectors obtained by independently choosing zero or $|F|$ as the coincidence coefficient. Every such covector for an active cap is strictly negative at $e$. Positive cap mass implies that some maximizing vertex lies strictly in the cap, so a relatively open part of an incident facet lies strictly in it, with positive area or an endpoint of counting mass one. All other coefficients are nonnegative.

A radial direction increasing total volume with all these cap covectors nonpositive would remain radial after adding a small positive multiple of $e$, still increase volume, and strictly decrease every active budget. Small positive steps retain slack budgets by continuity, contradicting local maximality. The finite Farkas alternative therefore puts $L_0$ in the cone generated by the active cap covectors and the negatives of the active rows. Group the cap generators into a nonnegative $\lambda_j$ and their convex average $L_j$. The dilation direction $h$ annihilates $A_0$ by homogeneity and has $L_0(h)=dM>0$, so some $\lambda_j>0$.

For a fiber translation by $c$, and respectively for its dilation about zero, apply the constant and radial divergence identities to a proper cap truncation. The cap section has outward normal $-u_j$, so the contributions to $L_j$ are $s_{jz}u_j\cdot c$ and $d|K_z\cap(H_j)_z|+t_j(z)s_{jz}$. In an inside coincidence, apply the full-body divergence identity and remove fraction $1-\theta_{jzF}$ of the facet flux with normal $-u_j$. In an outside coincidence only the fraction $\theta_{jzF}$ of the coincident facet with normal $u_j$ remains, and retained volume is zero. Strict full or empty cuts and lower-dimensional contacts use the full or zero divergence. These yield the same two formulas at every status. The affine translations $c_z=Bz+c$ are lineality because they preserve all anchored combinations, and $L_0$ vanishes there. Testing the identity on them yields the first two balances. Testing on $h$ yields the Euler equation.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite nonempty set of bases, and $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, full-dimensional compact polytopes compatible under every anchored convex combination on $P$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of their $d$-volumes, $M$ its total, and fix finitely many closed caps $H_j=\{v_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x\ge b_j\}$ with $|u_j|=1$ and budgets $\mu(H_j)\le B_j$. Suppose the family locally maximizes $M$ in the compatible support chart below subject to those fixed budgets, and every active budget has positive cap mass.

For each fiber use the normal fan of $K_z\ominus tB_d$ for all sufficiently small $t>0$. Take a common simplicial refinement, and restrict ray supports to the linear subspace where each fiber support is linear on its own chosen fan. Let $A_0$ be the active homogeneous support-convexity and compatibility rows there. For each original facet $F$ let $n_F$ be its unit outward normal and $|F|$ its $(d-1)$-area. The total volume derivative in any radial direction $\delta$ is $L_0(\delta)=\sum_{z,F}|F|\delta_z(n_F)$. For a noncoincident facet the cap derivative term is $|F\cap\operatorname{int}(H_j)_z|\delta_z(n_F)$. On a coincident facet the term is $|F|\min(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when the body lies in the cap and $|F|\max(\delta_z(n_F),0)$ when it lies on the outside. There exist nonnegative $\lambda_j,\eta$, with some $\lambda_j>0$ and $\lambda_j=0$ on slack caps, such that on the entire restricted chart
$$
L_0=\sum_j\lambda_j L_j-\eta^\top A_0 .
$$
Here $L_j$ uses the exact noncoincident coefficients and a coefficient $\theta_{jzF}|F|$, $0\le\theta_{jzF}\le1$, at each coincidence.

Put $t_j(z)=b_j-v_j\cdot z$. Define $s_{jz}$ as proper section area on a proper cut, zero at strict full or empty cuts and lower-dimensional contacts, $(1-\theta_{jzF})|F|$ at an inside coincidence, and $\theta_{jzF}|F|$ at an outside coincidence. With the same choices,
$$
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j s_{jz}u_j=0,\qquad
\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j s_{jz}u_j z^\top=0,\qquad
dM=d\sum_j\lambda_j\mu(H_j)+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_j t_j(z)s_{jz}.
$$
If all active masses are $\beta M$, the last identity is $1=\beta\sum_j\lambda_j+\sum_{j,z}\lambda_jt_j(z)s_{jz}/(dM)$. Facet and section areas in $d=1$ use endpoint counting.
title: Normalized support stress at a polytopal fixed-cap volume maximum
